text: The delivery fact is read on rwb-source-data's ACE-data contract for v_ace_pod and the notice with its served result on rwb-comms' contract. rwb-litigation holds no v_ace_* grant and owns no notice row, so the step writes no business row: its only durable effects are the decision record, the workflow state and the notice-period timer, and its answers to rwb-case carry the move, the case-stage timer and the officer task. No sixth REST operation is added to the five of TSD S4 T-A.1.
why: FEAT-LIT-02 names v_ace_pod as the source and 'writes it onto the notice', but the ownership rows of rwb-litigation name only hearing and legal_action, neither of which carries a served result or a delivery date, and the notice row is P6's; declaring a v_ace_* read would break the grant boundary of DP-05 and inventing a delivery operation would widen the five owned operations.
read: Context pack ownership rows of S4; TSD S4 T3.1 and T-A.1; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row FEAT-LIT-02; FSD S4 A2.2; legacy RWB-E5-002 data and endpoints tables; Architecture v5 slides 8 and 10 in the context pack (ACE data through the owner, Notices to rwb-comms).
confirm: Solution architect of S4 with the P1 and P6 architects for the two consumed contracts
impact: If rwb-litigation turns out to hold a v_ace_pod grant or P6 publishes a delivery operation, the two consumed rows change their owner and the boundary test is relaxed; no story or lane changes.

text: PROOF_OF_DELIVERY_RECEIVED, PROOF_WINDOW_EXPIRED and DELIVERY_FAILED are read as the names of workflow signals and state-machine events, not as Kafka subscriptions: the proof arrives on the rwb-source-data contract, the case read and the case-stage answer travel on the rwb-case contract, and this legacy key publishes and consumes no event.
why: The Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 and the Temporal design name an event per rule, while the ownership rows give rwb-litigation zero events, the FSD declares no background event and DP-09 is not in the pattern set; a consumer or a producer invented here would put a topic, an inbox and an event catalogue entry into a service the ownership map gives none.

text: The proof window of 7 days and the notice period are two durable timers of LitigationWorkflow: the first starts at dispatch, the second at delivered_at under R-LIT-07 and never under R-LIT-08 or R-LIT-09. The notice period is a versioned reference row per product and notice type whose content is not published; when the row is missing the step records the decision, holds the timer and answers no move. The case-stage timer and the officer task stay rwb-case's rows, requested on the stage outcome.
why: The timer row of the legacy data table is P3's and the pack gives S4 no job but one workflow, while the litigation clocks run for years and must survive releases; the notice period has no value in any source, so it cannot be a constant and must be a reference row that can be absent.
read: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-07 and R-LIT-08 timer columns; context pack Jobs (0), Workflows (1) and Temporal and Drools slide 7 notes; TSD S4 T5.3 and T6; legacy RWB-E5-002 data table (timer DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036); FSD S4 A2.3.2 (Quartz replaced by Temporal).
confirm: Business owner of the notice period with the S4 and P3 solution architects
impact: If the notice period must be a case-service timer, the answer to rwb-case grows a duration field and the workflow drops one timer; if the values arrive late, only the reference data changes.

text: Both stories trace to FEAT-LIT-02 and to REQ-S4-001, 'Demand and recall notices are generated by rule, approved, dispatched, and their notice periods are timed', with the reading stated in section 18, and the PRD column stays Pending (C1) until the Epics 3 to 8 PRD adds an identifier for the proof of delivery.
why: The legacy master of RWB-E5-002 and the Epics 3 to 8 specification carry no requirement identifier for this feature and the FSD S4 requirements table names no proof-of-delivery requirement; writing an identifier by pattern would create a reference no owner approved and no requirement trace can resolve.

text: The LITIGATION package is consumed from rwb-decision as a non-blocking contract with its fake, at its version in force, and the embedded rules runtime stays a service-template capability of the platform. Neither story declares a rule row, a package or a rule version of its own, and the metadata rows of both stories keep Contract dependencies None.
why: The three rules cannot be evaluated without the package, but DP-04 is not in the pattern set of this key and no dependency row exists for its two contracts; authoring the package here would take rule governance away from rwb-decision and duplicating the rows would let the rule and the story drift.
